reviews.title: Money-driven splash screens pretend to be apps
reviews.text:
I have been using Photoshop for 26 years, since 1994, and I have been paying for Adobe CSS every month for 10 years. yet I still have to sign in and input my password and wait for the 6-digit security code and input the code from my phone and then, apparently re-download the app only to see that I need to buy ANOTHER APP- Fresco or Adobe Photoshop Fix or Photoshop Mix or whatever among the 40 plus apps that Adobe pushes without ever allowing me to USE these apps on my desktop or my iPad or my iPhone. I still am shut-out from these apps by purchase screens in spite of the AUTOMATIC- CREDIT CARD DEDUCTIONS THAT HAPPEN EVERY MONTH!

It used to be easy to launch Photoshop and use it. Period. Buy an updated version every two years. NOT NOW. I can never use Photoshop in spite of paying for CSS every month. I am always buffetted with screens that wait for another subscription on top of the CSS subscription that I already pay for every month. Evil shameful Adobe execs that must have their own islands funded on the backs of aspiring artists and retired Photoshop teachers like me who can scarcely afford to continue subscribing to an endless avalanche of new apps that supersede the ones I am already paying for.

Here I am writing this instead of actually making art — typical of what we have learned to accept from these piggy companies.

Maybe you work in an office where someone else takes care of the subscriptions and all you need to do is log on and go. Sweet. So happy for you. For the

reviews.title: When I was a kid, we had Tinker Toys
reviews.text:
When I was a kid, we had Tinkertoys. Today, my kids have Photoshop. It’s so reassuring knowing they can spend hours making Minecraft photo edits without any supervision from me whatsoever. I was actually going to hire a babysitter while I went downtown to sell d$@g$, but thankfully that expense is no longer necessary. I have Photoshop!

I do feel a little bad for any professional trying to use it for legitimate work, but honestly, who cares? This review is about me and my beautiful new childcare solution.

Thanks, Adobe! Five stars for keeping the kids occupied while apparently making professional workflows somebody else’s problem.

Came back to double down on everything I said! Also, the removal tool comes up operation failed for all pictures, SFW. Then it tells me cloud storage is full but doesn’t allow me to delete anything. For this price and the fact that I was charged for two years for something I never ordered, plus the pain that the removal tool is, I can’t recommend the product.

reviews.text: been using photoshop for almost 20 years. got an ipad so that i could digital paint on the go only to find out some very basic features in desktop PS that are also standard in any other paint app, are completely missing. You can import .psd files from the computer and they will have fill layers, effect layers, etc in this iPad version but you can’t change any of their settings and you can’t make the effects in the app. Like the functionality is there but they deliberately handicapped this version of photoshop. PS brush settings are already pretty limited compared to most other paint apps, but in this version THERE ARE NO BRUSH SETTINGS! your only option is to import brushes, but if you want to modify anything other than the size of the brush, you need to make those changed on a computer and manually export them back over to the ipad. pretty ridiculous feature to be missing from the most expensive “industry standard” photo and digital paint software… I see why procreate is taking over.

There are no workarounds. If it doesn’t like where you want to put things, you cannot put them there. Also, this app really needs some quality finesse. There are numerous bugs that have existed and are easily reproducible for years. E.g., it constantly crashes, like whenever the screen auto-locks. Then there are numerous ways where features will stop working, and the only way to get it working again is to force-quit the app. Update: after another update, it’s clear there’s been an attempt to refresh the app. Now it’s worse than it’s ever been. None of the many years-old bugs have been fixed, new ones have been introduced. Update: re: dev response to post the bugs in a forum. How about Adobe devs try using their own product for an hour? They’ll find dozens of bugs. Don’t make your paying customers do your QA testing. Update: still bad. Update: almost unusable at this point. Update: how does this get worse? Liquidize tool size can only be powers of 2 from the slider. Tapping a different tool then go back to the previous tool and it shows the “real” tool size. This has been a bug for at least 6 months. reviews.title: Cannot move past home screen
reviews.text: Within the last week after opening Photoshop the program will only load the first 25 or so thumbnails in my files, leaving all available to scroll but freezing the app if I attempt to open any of them. If I try importing a file or photo, it will either freeze the app entirely again or give me a blank menu with contents that won't load. If I manage to tap the import button just quick enough after the splash screen, it allows me to open an image and create a new file - yet for whatever reason I am totally unable to use the transform mode, and who knows what other tools. Yes, I have uninstalled and reinstalled. This has made simple tasks nearly impossible given that I can't even access the service or my files 90% of the time. Between this (among other bugs) and Illustrator not having so much as a shear feature in 2026, it is becoming difficult to justify my Adobe subscription.

reviews.title: Works great when it ACTUALLY WORKS
reviews.text:
When it’s functional it’s the only app I want to use to draw on here. The pen is smooth and the linework looks nicer than anything else I’ve tried. 
Unfortunately it does NOT always work. Sometimes it decides it has random issues with specific files and decides to not let you open them. In an error pop up that literally reads “continue reading the document?” There is no way to force it open regardless of whichever layer is the issue. In a file with over a hundred layers, I couldn’t care less about one - especially when I know it’s not even in use. 
Also sometimes it just crashes because it can and when you reopen you’ve lost twenty minutes of work. 
If you want to pay for it, use with absolute caution is my advice. It’s lovely when it works but Photoshop, and just adobe really, is your enemy when it doesn’t.

reviews.title: Decent for Photo Editing. Abysmal for Painting.
reviews.text: To those reviews saying that this iPad app is anything close to the desktop version are either lying, paid, or woefully unfamiliar with the desktop app. While it does offer a number of features found in the desktop version, this is NOT a direct port. There are many often-used features missing which are available in other (LESS EXPENSIVE) iPad apps. Brush features leave a LOT to be desired. Editing brushes within the app is all but non-existent, offering very basic adjustments, and relying on .abr imports from either downloading from Adobe, or from brushes already owned from the desktop version. All in all, there are other apps that do offer direct comparison to their desktop counterparts. To Adobe: start listening to customers. Stop cramming AI into every aspect of the actual process of creating. Designers and artists don't want to "commission a robot." How the mighty have fallen, indeed.
